longterm_thesis:
One thesis runs through every brief since mid-September: at a ~5% risk-free rate and $365tn of global debt, the marginal dollar of capital stops buying narrative duration and starts buying physical chokepoints — electrons, molecules, memory bits, optics, copper, fissile fuel, refining capacity, and the skilled trades that install them. The demand driver is not an abstraction: humanity is trying to buy time and productivity via AI, and the bill for that is denominated in kilowatt-hours and DRAM bits, not in lines of code. Three separate briefs independently stamped the same conclusion — power, not silicon, is the binding constraint (Amazon's $8B Generac order, Meta funding seven gas plants, Mitsui contracting LNG for data centres, ERCOT's 2030s demand curve, Italy reversing a 40-year nuclear ban, Duke and Constellation raising guidance). That is a recurring, strengthening shift, not a headline. Energy and compute are converging into a single asset class, and generation/grid/behind-the-meter equipment owners get pricing power they have not had in decades.

The second durable shift is behavioural, and it is the most under-modelled: people are buying AI as *time*, not as intelligence. The fastest-rising consumer queries across three briefs are 'ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service', 'ai agent builder' — the delegation of the lowest-status use of a person's hours. Enterprises mirror this: they pay for measurable labour substitution (Copilot at 30M seats) and punish per-seat software that cannot show it (Adobe, Wix). The corollary is that inference migrates toward devices and edge silicon for cost, latency and privacy (Apple's cost-per-token claim, Qualcomm orders, Nvidia-Perplexity on RTX PCs), which makes the terminal value of pure centralized GPU rental contestable even while near-term order books boom. Own silicon, memory, optics and distribution; be sceptical of compute landlords and of standalone model vendors without distribution.

The third shift is that security has replaced convenience as the premium good — energy security, supply-chain sovereignty, digital security, and now *agent containment*. A single cyberattack broke Boston Scientific's guidance; Nvidia, Palantir and Booz Allen restricting Anthropic models over data fears; Nvidia assembling 100+ partners around agent safety after rogue-agent incidents. Trust, identity, audit trails and kill switches become mandatory line items that did not exist three years ago — a permanent tax on every dollar of AI adoption, which structurally raises cost-per-unit of adoption and creates a growth adjacency for security incumbents (though pricing here is already rich: CRWD 88, PANW 83).

Fourth, the household adapts rather than resolves. At 7.45% mortgages the shock absorber is turnover: people renovate instead of relocate, rent longer, live multigenerationally, lengthen auto loan duration to defend a monthly payment, and trade down in the mid-tier experience economy. Housing undersupply persists as a pricing problem into the late 2020s because construction robotics is real but not this cycle. Meanwhile status migrates from home equity to portfolio equity and to ownership of scarce physical things — which grows brokerage/custody/advice intermediation and hard assets, while the demographic-scale need for eldercare advice, estate management and fraud protection becomes a monetizable category for scaled wealth platforms. Capital allocation conclusion: overweight power/grid/gas-into-compute, memory and optics, edge silicon, agentic software with distribution, security, and financial intermediation; underweight anything whose moat was cheap capital — marginal housing, levered consumers, REIT roll-ups, second-tier AI capex and 'big dreams, tiny revenue' IPO supply.

memo.summary: This book is a barbell: 24% in AI-infrastructure/AI-software momentum (MU, NVDA, PLTR), 24% in a cheap-but-unloved energy complex (EOG, COP, OXY), a new 5% healthcare quality-value starter (DXCM), and a defensive 47% in cash, duration, gold, credit and commodities. The regime read — moderate expansion, sticky inflation, neutral liquidity, with contraction probability up 6 points to 27.6 and reflation down 6.2 — argues for exactly this hedged stance, and flows corroborate the tech leg (Technology flows accelerating, sector rotation +68, Growth leading Value by 89 points). The honest tension is that we are running 53% equity against a 62% recommended posture with 18% cash versus a 9% recommendation, i.e. the system is more cautious than its own risk score (54, 'Stable') says it needs to be, while simultaneously holding its three largest equity positions through valuation models that label MU (-19% expected return) and PLTR (-75.8%) exit candidates. In plain terms: we are overriding absolute valuation with momentum, flows and long-term theme conviction on the tech leg, and overriding momentum with valuation and theme conviction on the energy leg. Both overrides cannot be right for the same reason, and the energy leg is the one currently losing money (all three below entry, RSI 37-41, sector rotation -3).

key_bets.why: The largest expectations gap in the book (reality 84 vs pricing 56, 28 points) on a genuine fundamental inflection: TTM revenue +167%, operating margin +43pts YoY, ROIC 74%. Stage-2 uptrend, technical score 100, 12% off the 52-week high after a 550% 12-month run. Post-earnings drift window is the next live catalyst. We are explicitly ignoring a valuation component of 13/100 and an 'exit_candidate' expected-return band on the view that memory/HBM pricing is outrunning consensus multiples.

Best risk-adjusted profile in the tech leg: the only one with both a build-band expected return (+15.9%) and a reasonable valuation component (60), vol 39 vs MU 77. Flagged a swap candidate on ER/vol (0.40 vs best available 2.22) and catalyst density is thin (36) — held for anchor exposure to AI Infrastructure, not for near-term edge.

Highest HFE score in the book (5.4, x1.24 multiplier) and the strongest 3-month relative strength (+46.5 vs SPY). Added 5%→8% on the risk-adjusted rebalance. This is a pure narrative/flows bet: valuation component is 0.0, expected return -75.8%, and the research brief carries an explicit trim flag (pricing 77 vs attention 52, disclosed put positioning). The position exists because momentum and theme trend (62) are intact, nothing else.

Cleanest version of the energy thesis: reality 68 vs pricing 48, revenue accelerating to +19.1% from +2.8%, 11x P/E, net debt/EBITDA 0.2x, and attention rising while unpriced (attention 81, the highest in the book). Also a swap candidate at ER/vol 0.22, lagging its sector, and technically not ready (stage 'emerging', RSI 38.8).

Highest-beta expression of the energy leg, upsized 5%→8%. Margin +12pts YoY and decelerating revenue decline, but conviction 6.4, entry label 'avoid for now', expected return -8.3%, and a 3.5% stop distance against 2.75% ATR — roughly 1.3 ATR of room. This is the position most likely to be stopped out on noise and carries a review flag citing the 5.33% 10-year.

The only holding where valuation (85) and momentum (100) agree: +36.2% expected return, accumulate band, FCF growth +146%, P/E at the 4th percentile of its own history, positive relative strength versus both SPY and sector. Offsets: catalyst score 9 (one inferred item), negative Health Care rotation, and no HFE score at all (x0.85 penalty). Started small at 5% deliberately.

concentrations: 48% of equity in two sectors — Technology 24% and Energy 24%; with 53% total equity weight that is roughly 90% of the equity book in two cyclical sectors.

AI as a single factor: AI Infrastructure 12.8% plus AI Software & Agents 7.2% = 20% of total capital, and NVDA's own thesis notes ~90% theme exposure. MU, NVDA and PLTR will correlate hard in a drawdown.

LNG & Energy Security triple-counted: EOG, COP and OXY are the same oil-price and energy-security bet at 24% of capital, all three below entry, all three with RSI under 42, all three in 'emerging' not confirmed uptrends.
High-volatility tail: MU (vol 76.5) and PLTR (vol 77.2) at 8% each — 16% of capital in names with ~77 vol percentile.

Growth/momentum factor tilt in the equity sleeve, consistent with Growth leading Value by 89 points, but it means the portfolio has no defensive equity ballast — Visa was sold out of the ranking and nothing replaced it.
Defensive sleeve is 47%: 18% cash, 13% Treasuries (IEF 7.8 / TLT 5.2), 6% gold, 5% credit, 5% commodities. The 18% cash is an unhedged bet that waiting is cheap.
biggest_risks: Valuation models and the position sizes are in open conflict. Three of the four largest equity positions carry 'exit_candidate' expected-return bands (MU -19%, PLTR -75.8%, COP -4.0%, OXY -8.3%). If the system's multiple-based fair values are even roughly right, we are long the most expensive part of the market at maximum single-name weight.

The energy leg has no flow support. Energy rotation is -3, the LNG & Energy Security theme trend has decayed from 58 to 47, and the theme-trend exit rule for EOG/COP sits at a 45 threshold against a 47 current reading. One more point of theme decay triggers rule-based exits on 16% of capital simultaneously.

Correlated stop-out risk. Average stop distance is 6%, but OXY sits 3.5% from its stop with 2.75% daily ATR and PLTR 5.3% with 3.56% ATR. A single 2-3% market down day could cascade several stops at once and leave the book near 35% equity involuntarily.

Contraction probability rose 6 points to 27.6 and is now the single highest regime state, while liquidity (-3.9) and inflation (-3.8) dimensions both deteriorated and rates rose +2.1. That mix is hostile to both legs of the barbell — high-multiple tech and commodity cyclicals.

Duration positioning fights the flows. We hold 13% Treasuries including 5.2% TLT while the flow summary explicitly says long-duration Treasury flows are decreasing and rates are drifting up; the OXY brief cites a 5.33% 10-year. The hedge may not hedge.
PLTR was upsized the same week the research brief flagged it for a trim. The rebalance rule and the qualitative brief disagreed and the rule won. That is a process risk, not just a position risk.
Single-name concentration in a 7-position book: five positions at 8% means idiosyncratic blow-up risk is material. MU is one day past earnings with no post-print consolidation history yet.
what_would_change_our_mind: Technology sector rotation falling below -30 for two consecutive weeks, or AI Infrastructure theme trend dropping under 45 from 59. Either triggers rule-based exits on MU and NVDA and converts the whole thesis.

Adverse regime probability (Stagflation + Contraction) crossing 55 from the current 49.9. Contraction alone has moved from 21.6 to 27.6 in 60 days; another move of that size breaches the regime rule across every holding at once.
LNG & Energy Security theme trend printing below 45 (currently 47, down from 58) — that is the live trigger on EOG and COP and would validate the market's refusal to re-rate energy.

MU's next print showing memory pricing or HBM demand rolling over, or operating margin change turning negative versus the -2% threshold. The 28-point gap thesis depends entirely on the margin inflection persisting.
PLTR failing to beat-and-raise. At 73x EV/Sales and 152x P/E with a 0.0 valuation score, the thesis has no re-rating path — only continued acceleration. A single in-line quarter breaks it.

A swap executing on NVDA or EOG: both are flagged against a best-available candidate at ER/vol 2.22 versus their 0.40 and 0.22. If that candidate persists through next recalibration, holding these two becomes an active opportunity cost we should stop paying.
DXCM confirming — positive MACD and Health Care rotation turning up would argue for taking the 5% starter toward a full 8% and funding it from the weakest energy name.
Cash being put to work. If the gap between 53% actual and 62% recommended equity persists while markets advance, the cash drag itself is the error, not the hedge.
memo.hedging_note: The hedge here is structural, not derivative: 47% sits in cash, duration, gold, credit and commodities, and beta target was trimmed from 1.10 baseline to 1.05. That is a sensible posture given contraction probability is now the highest single regime state. Two caveats. First, the 18% cash against a 9% recommendation is double-weight — it is an unstated market-timing call, and it is the single largest line in the book. Second, the 13% Treasury allocation is a poor hedge for this specific equity book: in a sticky-inflation, rising-rates outcome (inflation dimension -3.8 but rates +2.1, 10-year at 5.33% per the OXY brief) both tech multiples and long bonds fall together, which is exactly the 2022 failure mode. Gold at 6% and commodities at 5% are the more honest hedges against the stagflation branch (22.3%), and the energy leg itself functions as inflation insurance — which is part of why we tolerate its weak momentum. The clustered stops are doing a lot of unacknowledged hedging work; be aware that average 6% stop distance on a 53% equity book caps realistic drawdown near 3-4% of capital, but only if stops fill cleanly, which they will not in a gap.
watchlist: CRM (Salesforce) — opportunity 64, gap 13, technical score 88, long-term conviction 0.76, but conviction only 20.9. Trigger: conviction above ~35 or Cloud Computing flows moving ahead of Semiconductors in the flow ranking. It would be the natural funding swap against PLTR if the trim flag gets louder.

Advertising & Attention Platforms — the only starred theme and we own none of it. Trend 54 against pricing 38 is a 16-point unpriced gap, the cleanest mispricing the system has surfaced. Trigger: any name in the theme clearing the technical template with conviction above 40.

Cybersecurity — ranked first in flows, ahead of Semiconductors and Cloud Computing, and we have zero exposure. Our tech leg is entirely semis-plus-PLTR. Trigger: a cybersecurity name entering the ranking at opportunity above 65.

The unnamed ER/vol 2.22 candidate referenced in the NVDA and EOG swap flags. That is 5-10x the risk-adjusted expected return of what we hold. Trigger: identify it and size it before next recalibration.

Visa — exited this week on ranking, not on thesis failure. Trigger: Financials flows stabilising (currently flagged deteriorating) plus re-entry into the ranking. It was our only non-cyclical equity ballast.

The three energy names as a block, specifically LNG & Energy Security theme trend. Trigger: a print below 45 forces a decision on 24% of capital; better to pre-decide which one we keep (EOG, on the 20-point gap and attention 81) than to be rule-stopped out of all three.
